column2: My lords who hold land far from home have long sent their dues late and their excuses early. Those lands would be better ruled by one lord of our own people who lives among them and answers to me as a tributary. Who shall I set over the new colony?
On second thought, leave things as they are.

My liege has gathered all the lands of the realm that lie far from home into one colony and set me over it. The lords of those lands now answer to me, and I answer to my old liege only with a quarter of my income. It is a heavy charge, and a great honour.

My liege has gathered all the lands of the realm that lie far from home into one colony under [NewColonyRuler.GetTitledFirstName]. My lands lie within it, so from now on I answer to the colony's lord instead.
Our liege has gathered all the lands of the realm that lie far from home into one colony under [NewColonyRuler.GetTitledFirstName], who will rule them as a tributary.
All the lands of my realm that lie far from home are now one colony under [NewColonyRuler.GetTitledFirstName], who rules them in my name and pays me a quarter of the colony's income.
I will not fail the realm.
At least I was paid for the land I gave up.
You were paid §Y75§! gold and §Y25§! piety for each county given to the colony.
